scope: Read-only review of current root checkout addplot3 suffix boundary, source-literal tests, and original AT4-55/56 operations.
summary: The v3 code closes both identified lexical false-recognition paths within the bounded source scanner: it validates the byte after an optional plus, and skips a rejected suffix's balanced semicolon command or fails closed if unbalanced. New regression assertions require zero AddPlot descriptors for all malformed suffixes including 3++, while separately checking that following valid plots retain their outer axis ownership. This review does not claim GUI, PDF, visual, or full 3D acceptance.

prior_v2_blocker.v2_risk_scope: The malformed 3++ path produced a lexical AddPlot descriptor with option_range=None; it did not make any property editable. The risk was false recognition/navigation, not unsafe literal editing.
prior_v2_blocker.current_evidence: scientific_scan.rs lines 597-603 computes suffix_end after a possible plus and validates the following byte against whitespace, `[`, `{`, `(`, or `%`. A second plus is rejected and the whole command is skipped via command_semicolon or scan refusal. Lines 606-610 consume the optional plus only after validation. Tests lines 195-214 assert all malformed forms, including 3++, produce no AddPlot descriptor. Tests lines 240-283 include 3++ in balanced nested-control and unbalanced cases.

original_55_surface_gaussian.source_operation: First recognized addplot3 has literal samples=21 and domain=-2:2; proposed reversible literals are samples=25 and domain=-3:3.
original_55_surface_gaussian.evidence: Test lines 64-93 pins original SHA and CRLF, checks exact full AddPlot source range, applies samples/domain patches, verifies byte preservation and inverse, and refuses unsupported mark/domain y edits.
original_55_surface_gaussian.limit: This establishes bounded lexical literal editing only; it does not establish 3D surface semantics, geometry quality, rendering, PDF correctness, or native GUI acceptance.

original_56_parametric_helix.source_operation: First recognized addplot3 has literal samples=181 and domain=0:720; proposed reversible literals are samples=201 and domain=0:360. Parametric x/y/z body is byte-preserved; samples y remains unsupported.
original_56_parametric_helix.evidence: Test lines 95-119 pins original SHA and CRLF, checks exact full AddPlot range, applies samples/domain patches and inverse, and asserts samples y is unsupported.
original_56_parametric_helix.limit: This establishes bounded lexical literal editing only; it does not accept 3D parameterization visually or semantically and does not claim samples y editing.

bounded_at4_acceptance.shared_contract: The existing ScientificKind::AddPlot, axis-stack ownership, immediate option-group range, and existing literal whitelist are reused. No 3D property keys/defaults or full 3D semantic adapter are introduced.

reviewed_forms: Explicit coordinate form in test: \addplot3+[options] coordinates {...};
Bare and plus options forms with samples/domain/mark and opaque unrelated options.
valid_syntax_review.table_form: No explicit table-form unit test is present. Static inspection shows addplot3 recognition consumes only the immediate options group and then uses the existing balanced command-semicolon boundary without inspecting table contents; a form like `\addplot3[samples=21] table[x=x,y=y,z=z] {file.dat};` leaves only samples in the addplot option range and the table body uninterpreted. This is a coverage note, not a blocker or a request to add table semantics.
valid_syntax_review.candidate_identity: The recognized instance intentionally uses the existing generic AddPlot kind/range and parent_axis; there is no distinct 3D candidate type or visual-semantic claim.

root_test_execution.reason: Root owns rerunning mandatory Rust gates after the current root change.
